subject: Help computing and attaching studentized residuals

messages.author: 9c178f85bc1c037d
messages.subject: Help computing and attaching studentized residuals
parts:
Hi,

I've been using R for about a month, and have reached the point where
I would like to identify outliers within my sample and delete them.

If I did *NOT* need to run lm() by a categorical variable, I would
simply use the studres() from MASS:

linEst <- lm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, dataFr)
library(MASS)
studres(linEst)

Actually, I want to identify and eliminate outliers, so I did the
following:

dataFr$StudRes <- studres(linEst)
dataNoOut <- subset(dataFr, abs(studRes) < 2)

My question is how to do this by values of a categorical variable?

Suppose that in my data frame, dataFr, I have a categorical variable,
cat, that has values: "10", "15", "20", "25."

Following Wickham 2011 JSS, I define my model as:

mod <- function(df) {
lm( y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, df)
}

and then I use plyr as follows:

byCat <- dlply(dataFr, .(cat), mod)

For an individual category, the following works just fine:

studres(byCat$`10`)

I've tried the following (this does *NOT* work):

ddply(byCat, .($split_labels), studres)

I just do not see how to use plyr to apply studres().

Of course, my intention is to link the studentized residual to its
observation so that based on a criterion (like "outliers have absolute
value of studentized residual greater than or equal to two"), I can
delete the outliers.

Please help me apply studres() to the estimates of each "by-group" of
the categorical variable, and also link the studentized residual to
its observation in the data frame. Once that's done, I think I can
take it from there (eliminate the outliers, re-run the linear model,
collect coefficients, etc.).

Thank you very much, in advance, for your response(s).

-Eric

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: Help computing and attaching studentized residuals
parts:
Hi Eric,

1) I would advise you against this approach because it is
statistically unsound. It is much safer to use a method that is
robust to the effect of outlying observations like the rlm function in
MASS.

2) You are much more likely to get help if you provide a reproducible
example (https://github.com/hadley/devtools/wiki/Reproducibility) that
provides all the code and data needed to recreate your problem.

Hadley

parts:
Hi Prof. Wickham,

Thank you for your speedy reply! Regarding 1: Can I get away by
saying that some of my committee members are less comfortable with
IRLS/Huber M-Estimation, and are more comfortable with "trimmed" OLS?
Please consider the "trimming of outliers" followed by OLS as a type
of "sensitivity check" of rlm().

I found a data set to use as an example, so here is an example of what
I am hoping to accomplish:

library(MASS)
birthwt

# The dependent variable is birthweight: bwt
# The explanatory variables are age and last weight (of mother): age
& lwt
# The categorical variable is race, which has values: 1, 2, & 3

# 1. First, without plyr/categories:

bwmod <- function(df) {
lm( bwt ~ age + lwt, df)
}

# 2. Estimate the coefficients:
bwEst <- bwmod(birthwt)

# 3. Compute the studentized residuals--studres() is a part of MASS:
bwSR <- studres(bwEst)

# 4. Combine:
bwAll <- cbind(birthwt, bwSR)

# I can take it from here, although if anyone has suggestions on
favorite packages to tabulate coefficients for publication, I would
graciously receive them.

# Now, here are the estimated coefficients by the categorical
variable:

byRace <- dlply(birthwt, .(race), bwmod)

# This is where I am stuck. I can compute the residuals by level of
the catetorical variable:

studres(byRace$`1`)
studres(byRace$`2`)
studres(byRace$`3`)

# but there has to be a better way using one of the plyr family of
functions.
# Furthermore, I would like to associate the residual back to its
observation (Step 4 above).

# Thank you very much, again, in advance for assistance,

-Eric

messages.subject: Re: Help computing and attaching studentized residuals
parts:
I am trying to find the 85th quantile value across groups in a dataframe.

For example, I want to the find the 85th percentile price across each color group in the diamonds dataset.

require(ggplot2)
require(plyr)

data(diamonds)
ddply(diamonds, .(color), subset, price == quantile(price, .85))

which gives the results below, which are not what is expected. I'm looking for one row for each of the 7 colors, but some colors aren't listed, and some are listed twice.

Is this possible to do with plyr or tapply?

Thanks
